summary: Explains check mode for ad hoc commands: with `-C`/`--check`, Ansible reports what it would do without changing remote systems.
questions: How do I do a dry run of an ad hoc command?
Will check mode actually create files on the remote host?

answer_card.title: Dry-run ad hoc commands with check mode
answer_card.answer_md:
Add `-C` or `--check` and Ansible makes no changes on remote systems:
```bash
ansible all -m copy -a "content=foo dest=/root/bar.txt" -C
```
Here `/root/bar.txt` is not created or updated.
